texts: On day 631 of Year 2, the keepers of the East Row together collected the silken threads from the lanterns of the East Row at dawn.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water.
Mire-essence formed in the cauldrons by evening.
Hesper stored the mire-essence in three clay vessels.
The keepers of the East Row drew the stored mire-essence at sundown.
The keepers of the East Row lit the lanterns of the East Row with the stored mire-essence at sundown.
Tessa Brae collected forty of the fallen feathers at the base of the cliff in the morning.
Tessa Brae added the feathers to the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe took feathers from the feather bin.
Bevin Coombe scattered the ground feathers around the Stilllight Lantern at sundown.
The ground feathers warded the Stilllight Lantern against wraiths.
No wraith approached the Stilllight Lantern that night.

parse: (: s6_light_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_keepers_1) (And (Member (sk_light $x) light) (Agent (sk_light $x) $x) (Patient (sk_light $x) sk_lantern_1) (Instrument (sk_light $x) sk_mire_essence_1) (Time (sk_light $x) sundown) (Past (sk_light $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

q1_issues.issue: The descriptive participial modifier in "the ground feathers" is predicated of the group symbol as (Member sk_feathers_3 ground), the group-as-object reading the plural rules bar; a descriptive modifier on a plural must go through the per-member distribution rule, exactly as the same parse did for "the fallen feathers" at statement 56.

q2_gaps: day-of-year dating ("On day 631 of Year 2"): (Day <n>) is defined only as a day-of-month granularity inside a calendar date, so an ordinal day-index of a year (and a bare era year) has no distinct term

a bare MASS-noun subject of an episodic clause ("Mire-essence formed in the cauldrons by evening"): the "bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set" rule is stated for plurals only, so nothing decides between minting a witness and leaving the bare kind constant for a mass noun
review.notes: Otherwise faithful and careful: "together" correctly suppresses the per-member rule in S1 while the unmarked plural subjects in S5/S6 get group event + distribution rule, the "forty of the fallen feathers" partitive has the full superset/subset/Cardinality shape, and Around/Against are preposition-named obliques rather than coined heads. Two defensible judgment calls worth noting: "The Stilllight Lantern was lit" is read as an eventive agentless passive rather than a predicative adjective (the "was laminated" precedent supports it), and "boiled ... in sea-water" takes Location rather than the preposition-named (In ...).

issues.reason: Categorical statements bars it in terms: "a descriptive modifier or copular predicate on a plural always goes through the distributive rule ... and a bare (Member <group> <prop>) appears only for a property genuinely of the collection itself (its size, its name)", and `ground` is a participial property of each feather, not of the collection, so (Member sk_feathers_3 ground) asserts the group-as-object reading the plural rules forbid (the Resultatives plural note repeats the same bar verbatim).

gaps_confirmed: Day-of-year dating ("day 631 of Year 2"): the Time term lexicon defines (Day <n>) only as a day-of-month granularity inside a calendar date, so a day-index of a year — and a bare era year — has no distinct term.

Bare mass-noun subject of an episodic clause ("Mire-essence formed in the cauldrons by evening"): the "bare plural in an episodic clause is a specific set" rule is written for plurals only, and the "a bare mass stays a constant" line is stated for an oblique's object NP, so nothing decides between a witness and the bare kind for a mass subject.
new_gaps: Collective "together" on a definite plural encoded as a single group witness: the prescribed collective form is "one event with multiple Agent atoms", which presupposes enumerable conjuncts; with one group symbol the marker leaves no positive trace at all and survives only as the absence of a distribution rule, so "the keepers together collected X" and a plain collective group predication are not distinguishable in the emitted atoms.

A per-member distribution rule over a plural subject copies a plural-GROUP object verbatim into each member's Skolem event — "The keepers lit the lanterns" yields (Patient (sk_light $x) sk_lantern_1), i.e. each keeper lit every lantern — so the only licensed distributive form over-asserts what is naturally a cumulative reading; every exemplified case (Coopers/the barrel, the kegs, the students) has a singular definite object or none, and a licensed form would need to carry "each member acted on some share of the object group".
adjudication.defect_summary: Statement 92 should be the per-member distribution rule (: s12_feather_ground (Implication (PartOf $x sk_feathers_3) (Member $x ground)) (STV 1.0 0.9)) — exactly the shape this same parse used for "the fallen feathers" at statement 56 — so a compliant form is licensed and this confirmed issue files no gap.
adjudication.notes: Everything else checks out against the instruction set, including the two calls the reviewer flagged: "The Stilllight Lantern was lit" as an eventive agentless passive is licensed by the "the worktop was laminated" precedent under Names and casing, and "in sea-water" as Location matches the listed in/at/on default with the bare mass staying a constant. Note that (Member sk_mire_essence_1 stored) in S5 is NOT the same defect — its bearer is an ordinary mass witness, an individual, so Member is the right attachment there.
